### Pandas version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/index.html) of pandas.

- [ ] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [main branch](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/getting_started/install.html#installing-the-development-version-of-pandas) of pandas.


### Reproducible Example

```python
df = pd.DataFrame( [["A", "B", "C"], [True, True, False]] ).T
df.columns=["strings", "ids"]
df["strings"] = df.strings.astype("string[pyarrow]")
df.loc[df.ids, "strings"] = df.loc[df.ids, "strings"]
```


### Issue Description

`df.loc[df.ids, "strings"] = df.loc[df.ids, "strings"]`

Below is the Exception.

comments:
What I think happened:

At location: `pandas/core/internals/managers.py:1369`
`new_mgr = col_mgr.setitem((idx,), value)`
Here the index was converted to a tuple of numpy array.

At location: `pandas/core/arrays/arrow/array.py:938`
`key = np.asarray(key)`
Here the tuple of array was converted to a 2D numpy array.

Finally at: `pandas/core/arrays/arrow/array.py:939`
`indices = np.arange(n)[key]`
Here the 1D array was indexed using a 2D array, resulting in exception.

This looks to work on main. I don't think we have a test for this but could use one

```
In [7]: pd.__version__
Out[7]: '2.1.0.dev0+379.g4e4688f5bf'

In [8]: df = pd.DataFrame( [["A", "B", "C"], [True, True, False]] ).T
   ...: df.columns=["strings", "ids"]
   ...: df["strings"] = df.strings.astype("string[pyarrow]")
   ...: df.loc[df.ids, "strings"] = df.loc[df.ids, "strings"]
```

Thanks! I guess I need to update to pandas 2.0 ASAP then :D
(I was silly and thought main means pandas 1.5.3)
Hey, does this issue need help?
